items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: We had a boy named Philander Tiller from Little Rock who I had recommended to join the band.

ctx.x: We stayed in that hotel. We didn't have money to pay for food -- to pay for food. And Mr. Dent, everytime that dinnertime come, he'd say, 'Come on, boys, and sit at the table. Come on out here and eat.' And he would feed us. And I can remember how we got out of that town. We had two saxophones in the band then. We had a boy named Philander Tiller from Little Rock who I had recommended to join the band. Fernando Tiller had been going to Howard University, and this particular year he had laid out of school.

So, in order to get out of town, Johnny Brown booked our band back to Sheffield, Alabama. And the only way he could do it was to take Phil Tiller's saxophone and ask him would it be all right for us to pawn his horn -- pawn Tiller's horn, and

let Tiller stay there.
And we would go to Sheffield, Alabama where Johnnie Brown had friends, and we had booked ourselves in there for several dances in and around Sheffield. And we pawned the horn for enough money to pay our train fare from there to Sheffield.
As luck would have it,
(Unintelligible) we played a big dance there. We had a big crowd. And Johnnie Brown was able to borrow money from one of the big business people there. He wired the money to Phil Tiller, paid up our bill there, and sent Phil Tiller a…
